title: Virtualization for Large Lists
description: Render thousands of rows efficiently using virtualization libraries and native techniques.

data.text: Rendering a list of thousands of items creates thousands of DOM nodes. Even if each item is lightweight, the browser struggles with layout, paint, and memory. Virtualization solves this by rendering only the items visible in the viewport plus a small overscan.

data.title: Considerations
items: Fixed-height virtualization is simpler and faster because row positions are calculated mathematically
Variable-height virtualization measures items dynamically, which is more flexible but computationally heavier
Choose fixed-height when possible, especially for tables, log viewers, and chat messages

data.text: react-window is a lightweight, widely used virtualization library. It provides FixedSizeList and VariableSizeList components.

data.title: Virtualizing a Large Table
data.content: Render 10,000 rows without freezing the browser.

data.title: Provide a Stable Key
data.text: Always provide a stable key prop for each row. react-window reuses DOM elements aggressively. If your key changes, virtualization breaks and React will lose track of item state.
react-virtuoso is a modern alternative with first-class support for variable-height items, grouped lists, and smooth scrolling. It automatically measures item heights and handles dynamic content.

data.text: Overscan renders a small buffer of items above and below the viewport. This reduces blank space during fast scrolling but increases DOM nodes. Tune overscan based on item complexity and scroll speed.

data.title: Practice: Build a Virtualized List
data.description: Create a virtualized list component using react-window that renders 10,000 rows without performance degradation.
steps: Create an array of 10,000 mock items with stable IDs
Implement a FixedSizeList component with itemSize of 40
Add an overscanCount of 3 for smooth scrolling
Open React DevTools and verify only ~20 items are in the DOM
Measure scroll frame rate and adjust overscan if needed
data.expectedOutcome: The list scrolls smoothly at 60fps with only visible items plus overscan rendered in the DOM.

items.question: When should I use virtualization?
items.answer: Use virtualization for lists larger than a few hundred items or when items have complex rendering. For small lists, the added complexity is not worth it.

items.question: Can I use virtualization with dynamic content heights?
items.answer: Yes, react-virtuoso supports dynamic heights out of the box. react-window also supports variable sizes but requires more manual configuration.

items.question: Does virtualization break scrolling position on re-render?
items.answer: If you provide stable keys and avoid changing itemCount unnecessarily, virtualization libraries maintain scroll position correctly.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Virtualization renders only visible items plus overscan
react-window is lightweight and ideal for fixed-height lists
react-virtuoso supports variable heights and grouped lists
Stable keys are critical for virtualization to work correctly
Use virtualization for lists larger than a few hundred items
